one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls in Oct 2-31: FY26 Q4 results come in early December, and the defendants' response to the consolidated securities class-action complaint is due Nov 4 (10-Q), both outside the window. The big event has just happened: the Sep 30 Investor Day (FY27 guide of $11.1-11.2B revenue and $19.04-19.12 non-GAAP EPS, versus consensus of about $10.81B and $17.81), plus the AWS ($1B+) and OpenAI deals, sent the stock up 10-13% on Oct 1. The stock is now about 31% above the ~$375 where the CEO sold on Sep 15. Two short-horizon effects pull against each other. Drift after a guidance surprise, analyst target raises (e.g. HSBC to Buy at $700) and the new ~$1B buyback support the price. Reversal after a sharp two-week run-up, and holders selling into strength (as after the August beat, when the stock fell about 10% in a week), weigh on it. I treat these as roughly offsetting: median about $489, slightly below spot, with monthly sigma of about 13% (45%/3.5), so the spread is roughly symmetric in log terms.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% P/E (FY28E non-GAAP EPS of $22.5 x 25x = $562) and 40% FCF yield net of SBC (FY28E FCF of $3.7B minus ~$1.05B SBC, at a 3.0% yield, less ~$4.5B net debt, over 189M shares = $443). Both are values as of Oct 2027.

inputs_detail.derivation: $19.08 x 1.18. I haircut growth to 18%, below the mid-20s target, because management missed its Design IP guidance in 2025 (which led to the class action), because SBC (~$950M) and amortization are excluded from the non-GAAP figure, and because part of the EPS growth comes from buybacks.

The stock trades at about 25.7x FY27 guided EPS today ($490.54/$19.08). Cadence trades at about 41x forward. Before the rally SNPS traded at about 19x forward EV/EBITDA, below its 22x average (TIKR). I hold about 25x and do not re-rate toward Cadence, given ~$10B gross debt, an SBC-heavy non-GAAP measure, and China/export-control exposure.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $3.7B less SBC ~$1.05B = $2.65B; 3.0% yield gives EV $88.3B; less net debt ~$4.5B; 189M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.1B x ~1.2, below the mid-20s FCF CAGR target.
FY26 guided SBC grown about 10% a year, treated as a real cost.
$10.04B debt minus $3.61B cash = $6.4B at Jul-2026; plus ~$3.1B FY27 FCF, minus ~$1.5B buybacks (up to 50% of FCF; $1B near-term program), minus other uses.
191.6M outstanding at Jul-2026; the $1B buyback (~2M shares) is partly offset by SBC dilution (the count rose from 186M at Oct-2025).
Quality EDA duopoly with high-teens growth targets. I use 3.0% rather than the ~2.5% implied by Cadence's premium, to reflect leverage and execution risk.

bear.story: The Investor Day targets prove too high. Design IP disappoints again on AI customization economics (the 2025 pattern), AI chip-design spend digests, or China export controls on EDA come back (they were imposed in May 2025 and rescinded in July; China is ~10% of revenue). FY27 EPS lands near $17.5, and the multiple compresses to about 19-20x as the class action proceeds and leverage looks heavier.

base.story: FY27 broadly delivered (~$18.8-19.1 EPS) and the market looks to FY28 EPS of about $22.5 at about 23-25x. The buyback offsets some dilution. The class action goes through motion-to-dismiss with no material cost. The AWS and OpenAI deals help but do not yet prove that the business model has changed.

bull.story: AI-agent monetization and application-optimized IP (AWS as lead customer) show up in the numbers. EDA reaches 13%+ and IP 17%+ growth, margins head toward 50%, FY28 EPS reaches $24 or more, and the multiple re-rates toward 30x, closer to Cadence.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $360, the stock would have given up the whole Investor Day re-rating and fallen through the 52-week low ($362.55). That would likely mean the FY27 guide ($19.04-19.12 EPS, ~$11.15B revenue) has lost credibility, through a renewed Design IP miss, reinstated China EDA export restrictions, or AI design-spend digestion, rather than ordinary 45%-vol noise. At that level the market would be paying about 19x a guide it no longer believes.

key_uncertainties: Whether the Investor Day targets are credible, given management missed its Design IP outlook in 2025 (36% one-day drop and class actions)
China export-control policy for EDA (China ~10% of 9M FY26 revenue; restrictions imposed and lifted within weeks in 2025)
Size of the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP (FY27 GAAP EPS $8.16-8.61 vs non-GAAP $19.04-19.12) and SBC dilution
Whether AI chip-design spending holds up, and whether agentic-AI monetization actually changes pricing
Exit multiple: 25x vs Cadence at about 41x forward; a re-rating either way dominates the outcome
Reversal risk after a ~31% two-week run-up into and after Investor Day
reasoning: Basic facts: FY26 guide of $9.69-9.74B revenue and $15.04-15.10 non-GAAP EPS; $10.0B debt against $3.6B cash; 191.6M shares; $10.9B backlog. At the Sep 30 Investor Day the company guided FY27 to ~$11.15B revenue, $19.08 EPS and $3.1B FCF, about 3% and 7% above consensus, and set FY26-30 targets of ~15% revenue CAGR, mid-20s EPS/FCF CAGR and a ~50% margin. The stock re-rated from ~$375 (Sep 15, when the CEO sold under a 10b5-1 plan) to $490.54. As the skeptic, I looked for what could make consensus (22 of 24 analysts Buy) wrong on the downside. (1) Credibility: the 2025 Design IP miss caused a 36% one-day drop and securities and derivative suits that are still live (consolidated complaint due Sep 23; response due Nov 4). (2) Accounting quality: non-GAAP excludes ~$950M SBC and large Ansys amortization, so GAAP margin is about 10% vs non-GAAP 41.5% and the share count is rising despite buybacks. (3) Leverage: ~$10B of BBB+ notes from the Ansys deal, maturities starting April 2027. (4) China/export controls: in 2025 the US imposed an EDA license requirement and lifted it within six weeks, and the August 2026 sell-off was partly fear of a repeat. (5) Sell-side bears earlier in 2026 (Morgan Stanley and HSBC downgrades) cited slowing core EDA growth and muted IP. Weighing this honestly: the FY27 guide is backed by a large backlog and a $1B+ AWS contract, and at ~25.7x guided FY27 EPS the stock is not expensive against Cadence (~41x). The bear case is therefore mainly an execution and multiple risk, not a solvency or fraud risk. I found no short-seller report. My blended fair value of $514 (P/E $562, SBC-adjusted FCF $443) is slightly above spot, and the scenario mean is about $525. I set the ladder as a lognormal with median ~$505, below the scenario mean because of skew, and sigma ~0.38, a little under the 45% realized vol, which was inflated by event jumps. I fattened the left tail slightly for the history of guidance misses and binary export-control risk. Research limits: Seeking Alpha and Benzinga blocked fetching (403); some secondary data aggregators (MarketBeat, StocksToTrade) are low quality and were used only for corroborated facts. No option data was consulted.
